status: Validated math variants; modest direct GPU gain, no complete-preview CPU adoption win
controls: Reference shader and uniform/resource setup retained; CPU setSubmitPixels(false) skips only glDrawArrays. Complete control still clears/updates/presents a transparent surface.
conclusions: Fast atan not a consistent improvement over built-in
Two-step precomputed variant lowers two single-layer 2x private-pass GPU medians about 7-11% in three repeats
Full-path CPU highly variable and remains expensive even with actual draws disabled
History benchmark with two-step kernel does not consistently beat production snapshot history
limitations: No live module or default renderer change
Quality is vs current analytic shader, not approval of known NanoVG appearance differences
No-draw control is not a pure additive overhead measurement: deferred driver/GPU synchronization can differ
GPU/CPU clock effects and run-order variation are present; no universal percentage claim
